questions.stem: A 6 months child presented with diarrhoea and vomiting for three days. Which of the following enterotoxin is most likely responsible for the condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
NSP4

The rotavirus non-structural protein NSP4 was the first viral enterotoxin discovered. It induces diarrhoea and causes Ca2+-dependent transepithelial secretion.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 533

questions.stem: All of the following are true about rotaviral gastroenteritis except:

options.label: A
options.text: The name of the causative agent was suggested by its appearance

options.label: B
options.text: Most cases of the disease occur in infants and children

options.label: D
options.text: The disease is transmitted by the faecal-oral route

questions.solutionHtml:
Rotavirus belongs to Filoviridae.
  • ROTAVIRUS: Rotaviruses resemble cartwheels with short spokes radiating from a wide hub to a clearly defined outer rim. The name is derived from rota, which in Latin, means- ing wheel. The complete or 'double-shelled' virus measures about 70 nm in diameter and has a smooth surface. Identified by Bishop and colleagues (1973) in Melbourne, rotaviruses are now recognised as the most common cause of diarrheal disease in infants and children. Divided into six groups (A-F) and 14 serotypes (9 humans, 5 animals) (option A)
  • The commonest cause of gastroenteritis in children below 2 years of age(option B)
  • Infection is transmitted by contaminated water and food(option D)
  • I.P.: 1-2 days, vomiting, diarrhoea, dehydration


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 564,565

questions.stem: Lipid envelope is found in which virus:
questions.solutionHtml:
Herpesvirus
  • Herpesvirus is an enveloped virus. The rest of the options are non-enveloped. (options A and C)


Apurba Sastry 3rd Edition Page No. 81, 424; Ananthanarayan 12th Edition Page No.73, 498

questions.stem: A patient comes to the clinic with a complaint of multiple episodes of loose watery stool for 5 days. He gave a history of shellfish consumption at a local restaurant 5 days back and other people who had food from the same restaurant had similar symptoms. This viral gastroenteritis agent has a segmented, double-stranded RNA genome and is Non-enveloped. It is a member of which virus family?
questions.solutionHtml:
Reoviridae

Icosahedral virions, nonenveloped, segmented genome (10-12 segments), positive-stranded ds RNA



Ananthanarayanan 12th Edition Page No. 564; Apurba Sastry 3rd Edition Page No. 82,83

questions.stem: A 3-year-old boy presents in Paediatric OPD with complaints of watery diarrhoea, vomiting and fever. The child used to go to a daycare centre from where the same cases were reported two days back. Which of the following is the most common causative agent of gastroenteritis in this child?
questions.solutionHtml:
Rotavirus

All of the above-mentioned viruses can cause gastroenteritis.



Apurba Sastry 3rd Edition Page No. 424, Ananthanarayan 12th Edition Page No.498

questions.stemHtml: An outbreak of viral gastroenteritis occurred in a daycare centre. A stool sample was collected for laboratory diagnosis. On Immunoelectron microscopy, the virus gives a cartwheel appearance. Which of the following statement is true about the causative agent?

options.label: A
options.text: Virus isolate is a segmented dsDNA virus

options.label: D
options.text: Most common serotype in India is 19G.

questions.solutionHtml:
Belongs to the family Reoviridae.
  • Rotaviruses are the most common cause of diarrheal illness in children belonging to the Reoviridae family.
  • The incubation period is about 1–3 days. It has an abrupt onset, characterised by vomiting followed by watery diarrhoea, fever and abdominal pain (option C).
  • It is the only virus family with dsRNA (option A). The most common type seen in the world as well as in India is G1P[8] (option D).


Apurba Sastry 3rd Edition Page No. 424; Ananthanarayan 12th Edition Page No.498

questions.stem: A 3-year-old boy presents in Paediatric OPD with a complaint of watery diarrhoea, vomiting and fever suggestive of viral gastroenteritis which is vaccine-preventable. The vaccination schedule for the same is:
questions.solutionHtml:
At 6,10 and 14 weeks, orally

Rotaviruses are the most common cause of diarrheal illness in children for which two vaccines are available.



Apurba Sastry 3rd Edition Page No. 425; Ananthanarayan 12th Edition Page No.498

questions.stem: A Pregnant female presented with acute hepatitis. The serological test is negative for HBs Ag and positive for HEV antibody. What is the route of infection?
questions.solutionHtml:
Faecal-oral

HEV antibody is suggestive of Hepatitis E infection which is recommended-orally transmitted via sewage contamination of food and water.



Apurba Sastry 3rd Edition Page No. 488; Ananthanarayan 12th Edition Page No.530
